description:
We are ULTRON X, a multidisciplinary team of ENSIASD students specializing in Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Information Systems Management. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are developing Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive tool that uses NASA data to explore and compare potential lunar landing sites, analyzing terrain, solar visibility, and Earth communication opportunities.

ULTRON X — Think beyond Earth. Build beyond limits!
summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web-based tool designed to analyze and compare potential landing locations near the lunar south pole. It evaluates important environmental conditions, including Sun visibility, direct Earth visibility, periods of darkness, and local terrain obstructions.

Using astronomical data from NASA JPL Horizons and lunar elevation data from NASA's LRO LOLA dataset, the platform provides interactive visualizations and quantitative indicators to help users understand how lighting and direct-to-Earth visibility change over time.

Users can analyze individual locations, compare multiple candidate sites, and validate astronomical calculations against independent JPL Horizons results. The goal is to make preliminary lunar landing site assessment more accessible and data-driven, supporting the planning of future lunar exploration missions.
details:
Project Overview

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web platform designed to support the preliminary analysis and comparison of potential landing locations near the lunar south pole.

The project focuses on two important environmental factors for future lunar missions: sunlight availability and direct visibility of Earth. Local terrain can obstruct the Sun or Earth, creating periods without sunlight or direct visibility.

How It Works

Users select a lunar location and an analysis date range. The platform processes hourly astronomical data to determine whether the Sun and Earth are above the local horizon.

The platform provides several indicators:

  • Sun visibility percentage.
  • Earth visibility percentage.
  • Longest period without sunlight.
  • Longest period without direct Earth visibility.
  • Longest combined blackout period.
  • Current, mean, and maximum Sun elevation.
  • Time until the next sunset or Earthset, when applicable.

A polar sky plot and visibility timeline help users understand the results.

For locations with available terrain profiles, the platform uses lunar elevation data to estimate how surrounding terrain may obstruct the Sun and Earth. For locations without terrain profiles, it uses a clearly identified flat-horizon approximation.

Site Comparison and Scoring

The Compare section allows users to compare candidate locations over the same date range.

A weighted score combines Sun visibility and Earth visibility:

Score = (Sun weight × Sun visibility) + (Earth weight × Earth visibility)

The default weights are 60% for Sun visibility and 40% for Earth visibility. Users can adjust these weights according to their planning priorities.

This score is a preliminary planning indicator, not a probability of mission success.

Validation

The Validation section compares stored astronomical positions with independent NASA JPL Horizons queries for the same location and time.

The project also provides an indicative comparison with published lunar illumination research by Gläser et al. (2018).

Benefits and Goals

The platform helps users:

  • Explore environmental conditions at candidate lunar landing locations.
  • Understand how terrain can affect sunlight and direct Earth visibility.
  • Compare locations using consistent indicators.
  • Identify periods of darkness and direct visibility interruptions.
  • Make preliminary, data-driven comparisons for future lunar exploration planning.

Technologies and Tools Used

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Development of the web interface and interactive features.
  • Node.js: JavaScript runtime environment for executing scripts and server-side operations.
  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Code editor for developing, editing, and managing project files.
  • NASA JPL Horizons System: Access to astronomical ephemerides and celestial body position data.
  • NASA Moon Trek and LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Model: Access to lunar terrain information and elevation data.
  • GitHub Pages: Hosting and publishing the website.

Limitations

The results are intended for preliminary analysis, not operational mission certification. Terrain profiles are currently available only for selected locations. Other locations use a flat-horizon approximation. The calculations use hourly sampling, and actual communication link quality and usable solar power are not modeled.
